origin.title: A senior engineer who ships — and leads.
origin.p1: I'm Jorge Bastidas, the engineer behind decode9. Since 2014 I've designed and built software across the entire stack — from the infrastructure and data underneath to the interface founders demo to investors.
origin.p2: Today I'm also CTO at The Empire, where I lead the engineering behind products like Solvo, Finami and Desaparecidos Terremoto Venezuela — from the first architecture decision to production, and the teams that keep them running.
origin.p3: Whether you're validating an idea, scaling under load or drowning in manual process, the goal is the same: turn complexity into a system that works — and keeps working.

work.title: Real products, in production.
work.sub: Products I've led end to end — most of them built with The Empire.

the-empire.summary: The Empire is a product and digital-operations partner: it defines ideas before building them, then ships custom platforms, MVPs and AI agents. As CTO I lead the engineering behind its products and client platforms.
the-empire.challenge: Run several production products and client platforms at once — each with its own stack, team and uptime expectations — without the quality bar slipping.
the-empire.solution: One engineering playbook across every repo: layered architectures, infrastructure as code with Terraform, CI/CD quality gates and serverless AWS as the default runtime.
outcomes: Solvo, Finami and Desaparecidos built and operated in-house
Terraform + GitHub Actions deploys across products
The same standards from Blueprint to Platforms

solvo.summary: An AI sales agent for WhatsApp that knows each business's catalogue, stock, prices, calendar and orders. It qualifies, quotes, books and hands off to a person whenever money or judgement is involved.
solvo.challenge: An LLM that promises what the business can't deliver is a complaint generator. The agent had to act on real data without ever inventing prices, slots or payment confirmations.
solvo.solution: Fifteen tools that call the same use cases as the admin panel, guardrails enforced in code — every reply is checked against the database before it's sent — and a 13-state order flow where every change records its author.
outcomes: The AI can write exactly one order state, and only with explicit confirmation
Double-booking prevented by the database, not by a prompt
One isolated installation per client, provisioned on AWS with Terraform

desaparecidos.summary: A public platform to reconnect families after the La Guaira earthquakes of June 2026: report someone you can't reach, mark them as found, search by photo and follow live metrics — run by volunteers, funded through Latin Freedom.
desaparecidos.challenge: Go live within hours of a disaster, absorb a traffic spike driven by national and international press, and protect highly sensitive data — including photos of minors.
desaparecidos.solution: A static Next.js front end behind CloudFront and WAF, a Node API split into serverless functions, moderation with duplicate merging and three-stage verification, and photo matching through a partner face-recognition service where a human always confirms.
outcomes: Moved from EC2 to Lambda mid-crisis, then right-sized to cut infrastructure cost by ~60%
Minors' photos kept in storage that is never public
Read-only API with an OpenAPI spec for partner organizations

finami.summary: Two products under one brand: Finami App, a personal-finance app whose data is encrypted on the phone, and Finami Business, a multi-tenant financial ERP for invoicing, cash, accounting, inventory and credit.
finami.challenge: Offer sync and backups without the server ever being able to read someone's finances — and run a business ERP where tenants never see each other's data.
finami.solution: An offline-first mobile app with SQLCipher and end-to-end encrypted sync — the server only stores sealed records — plus a Postgres-schema-per-tenant SaaS with RBAC and 2FA, on hexagonal layers enforced by lint rules.
outcomes: The sync server can't read what it stores
A tenant's schema is created automatically on signup
CI publishes straight to the Google Play tracks

latin-freedom.summary: Latin Freedom trains, connects and funds citizens leading community initiatives across Latin America. I built its digital platform: the public site, donations, volunteering, the staff back office and the Tándem Ayuda landing.
latin-freedom.challenge: Accept one-off and monthly donations for a dozen campaigns on a Stripe account shared with other apps — and keep every dollar traceable.
latin-freedom.solution: One serverless API powering four apps, with donations and administration split into separate functions, a ledger reconciled against Stripe by scheduled workflows and per-campaign permissions checked on every request.
outcomes: An admin-side failure can't take donations down
Charges that arrive without a campaign are detected and tagged
WAF geo-blocking and rate rules in front of every app

patilla-games.summary: The video-game vertical of the Venezuelan news site La Patilla: a public catalogue, in-house games with Venezuelan identity, game jams with voting and ad revenue shared with developers — white-label ready for other media.
patilla-games.challenge: Publish third-party browser games safely, keep every game fast on 3G and pay developers fairly from ad revenue.
patilla-games.solution: Uploads land in a quarantine bucket before reaching the CDN, games run in sandboxed iframes on a shared TypeScript kit, and AdSense revenue is imported daily and split per game into a ledger with frozen rates.
outcomes: White-label builds proven byte-identical to the default brand
Every in-house game under 3 MB and playable in under 2 s on 3G
